citation: Sillito, J. and Kutomi, E. (2020). Failures and Fixes: A Study of Software System Incident Response.
source_verification: IEEE Xplore metadata and author-hosted arXiv full text
verified_evidence_summary: Qualitative analysis of 30 incidents: 15 collected through in-depth interviews with engineers and 15 sampled from public incident reports. The study examines how failures were detected, investigated and mitigated and reports practice observations about production support.
limitations_or_cautions: No controlled reliability-automation comparison and no validated workload, trust or decision-quality instrument identified in the accessible paper; interview and public-report sources have different evidential properties.

citation: Chan, C. and Cooper, B. (2020). Debugging Incidents in Google's Distributed Systems: How Experts Debug Production Issues in Complex Distributed Systems.
verified_evidence_summary: Reports research on how Google engineers debug production issues, including the tools, strategies and tasks used during investigations and common engineering journeys.
limitations_or_cautions: The accessible metadata does not establish a controlled automation comparison or direct validated workload/trust measure; organisation-specific context limits transferability.

citation: Grayson, M.R. (2020). Cognitive Work of Hypothesis Exploration During Anomaly Response: A Look at How We Respond to the Unexpected.
source_verification: ACM Queue record and ACM metadata
verified_evidence_summary: Discusses the cognitive work involved in exploring hypotheses during software anomaly response and is useful for terminology and human-factors citation chaining.
limitations_or_cautions: Retain as contextual material rather than peer-reviewed primary evidence unless the full text and publication status support a different classification; it does not establish an automation effect.

citation: Pope, M. and Sillito, J. (2024). Learning From Lessons Learned: Preliminary Findings From a Study of Learning From Failure.
source_verification: ACM DOI metadata and author-hosted arXiv HTML full text
verified_evidence_summary: Preliminary analysis of 13 incident reports and seven interviews with engineers, managers and product managers concerning how teams learn from failures and use lessons learned. The paper identifies social, situated and organisational aspects of incident learning.
limitations_or_cautions: Data collection and analysis were incomplete at publication; this is not a controlled automation comparison and the findings concern learning from failure rather than direct workload or trust effects.

citation: Dakkak, A., Bosch, J. and Holmström Olsson, H. (2022). Controlled Continuous Deployment: A Case Study From The Telecommunications Domain.
source_verification: Chalmers publication record and author-hosted full text
verified_evidence_summary: Derives a Controlled Continuous Deployment approach from an Ericsson case study involving three radio-access-network technologies in 3G, 4G and 5G embedded software. The approach explicitly considers high reliability and availability requirements and limited rollback after deployment; the work was discussed with Ericsson engineers through workshops.
limitations_or_cautions: Single industrial organisation and telecommunications domain; case-study evidence is not a controlled comparison of recovery strategies and workshop discussion is not a direct workload or decision-quality measure.
